about: The Summaries and Dictionary refusals and messages (T12.20): apps/desktop/src-tauri (summaries_tests.rs, summary_vocabulary_tests.rs, summary_style_tests.rs) runs every case through the app's own IPC functions, and packages/ui/src/ipc/mockSummaries.test.ts runs them through the mock, so the mock's copy of the Rust rules cannot drift. A settings case is `base` with `change` applied; `error` is the exact message (null when stored), `stored` the fields that differ from the input. Every name and word is invented. Generated once; edit by hand afterwards.

key_binding.about: T14.31: whether a saved Anthropic API key counts as saved with the Anthropic address `now` (provider Anthropic), when it was saved with the address `saved_for`. `saved_for` null is a key saved before T14.31 (no recorded address): it counts for the Anthropic API address only. Both suites save the key through their own key command with `saved_for` stored, then store `now` and ask whether a key is saved.

dictionary_adds.about: The Dictionary page's one-word adds and removals (T12.78): quotes at the ends of a typed entry (straight single and double, curly U+2018, U+2019, U+201C, U+201D) are dropped, repeatedly, and inner ones kept; an entry that is only quotes is not a word. Each case starts from `before` (stored as it is, the way an earlier version may have stored it), adds `add`, then removes `remove` when given; `added` says whether the add wrote, `word` is the entry as the Dictionary holds it, `stored` the list after both, `error` the add's exact message (nothing stored). Run through the app's IPC functions (summary_vocabulary_tests.rs) and the mock (mockSummaries.test.ts).

people.about: The saved people's names a summary may be given (T12.91; the Dictionary page lists none since T12.97, earshot_core::prompt::People::new over the saved names in the People page's order): each name on one line with white space joined, names that are empty, longer than 100 characters or hold a control or invisible formatting character left out, and a name that repeats an earlier one or a Dictionary entry in another case left out. Run through People::new (summary_vocabulary_tests.rs) and the mock's peopleOf (mockSummaries.test.ts). `left_out` is how many names were left out for what they hold (a control or invisible formatting character, or more than 100 characters; never empty names or repeats): People::left_out and the mock's peopleLeftOut, which the Dictionary page reports with messages.people_left_out (T12.91a). Every name is invented.
